title: Perplexity MCP Server
summary: Add Perplexity's official MCP server so your coding agent can run live web searches and get cited research answers while it works.
description: Perplexity's MCP server gives an agent four tools: ranked web search, quick conversational answers, deep research with citations, and step-by-step reasoning. It is useful when a library changed after the model's training data ended.

This setup runs the server locally through npx and reads your key from the PERPLEXITY_API_KEY variable. Perplexity also offers a hosted Streamable HTTP endpoint with OAuth sign-in, if you prefer no local process.
useWhen: Check the current release notes for a library before upgrading
Look for a known issue behind an error message you cannot place
Get a cited comparison of two tools before you pick one
Verify an API detail that may have changed recently

mcp.name: perplexity

env.name: PERPLEXITY_API_KEY
env.description: Your Perplexity API key, from your Perplexity API account

access: Sends your search questions and prompts to Perplexity's API, which bills your API key
Does not read or change local files

example.prompt: Use perplexity_search to find what changed in the latest Vite major release and list the breaking changes.
example.result: Top results point to the Vite release notes and migration guide. Breaking changes: the minimum Node version was raised, a plugin hook was renamed, and one default build target moved. Each item cites its source URL.

faq.question: Which tool should I ask for?
faq.answer: perplexity_search returns ranked links, perplexity_ask answers quickly, perplexity_research digs deeper with citations, and perplexity_reason handles logic problems.

faq.question: Is there a way to avoid the local process?
faq.answer: Yes. Perplexity documents a remote server at https://api.perplexity.ai/mcp that signs in with OAuth or a bearer API key.

faq.question: Does search_type fast matter?
faq.answer: Setting it on perplexity_search gives lower latency and cost. It needs local server version 1.3.0 or later.

access: Sends your queries to Perplexity and uses your API quota
